items.title: Why "Noble-Loved Precepts"; Right Effort, Mindfulness, and Concentration

items.zh: 何故此名聖所愛戒？答：以諸聖者、賢善、正至，長時愛樂、欣慕、悅意：我於何時當正獲得諸語惡行、諸身惡行、諸邪命事不作律儀？由彼長夜於此尸羅深心愛樂、欣慕、悅意，故獲得時，名聖所愛。獲得如是聖愛戒已，終不正知而說妄語，終不故思害眾生命，終不故思不與而取，終不故思行欲邪行，終不非法求衣服等。即由如是聖所愛戒增上力故，於修道時，乃至所有語業、身業、養命事轉，亦得名為正語、業、命。依止正見及正思惟、正語、業、命勤修行者，所有一切欲、勤、精進、出離勇猛、勢力發起、策勵其心，相續無間，名正精進。成就如是正精進者，由四念住增上力故得無顛倒九種行相所攝正念，能攝九種行相心住。是名正念及與正定。
items.en: Why are these called the noble-loved precepts? Answer: because noble ones, the good and worthy, those who have rightly arrived, have long delighted in, longed for, and taken joy in this very question — "when shall I rightly attain this restraint from verbal misconduct, bodily misconduct, and wrongful livelihood?" Because of this long-held delight in this discipline, when it is finally attained, it is called noble-loved. Having attained this noble-loved discipline, one never again knowingly speaks falsehood, never deliberately takes a being's life, never deliberately takes what is not given, never deliberately engages in sexual misconduct, and never seeks clothing and the rest by improper means. … Relying on right view, right intention, right speech, right action, and right livelihood, the diligent practitioner's every aspiration, exertion, courageous striving towards release, and continuous, uninterrupted spurring of the mind is called right effort. One who has accomplished such right effort, through the power of the four foundations of mindfulness, attains undistorted mindfulness comprised of nine aspects, sustaining the mind's abiding through those same nine aspects — this is called right mindfulness together with right concentration.

items.title: Section: The Eightfold Path Closes — and with It, All Thirty-Seven Factors of Enlightenment

items.zh: 如是一切八支聖道，總立二種。謂無所作及住所作。無所作者，謂正語、正業、正命。住所作者，復有二種。謂奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。正見、正思惟、正精進、是毘鉢舍那；正念、正定、是奢摩他。如是清淨正語、業、命為所依止，於時時間修習止觀，能斷諸結。無餘永斷，能得最上阿羅漢果。長時相續，名為修道，多時串習斷煩惱故。率爾智生，名為見道，暫時智起，即能永斷諸煩惱故。由是因緣，正語、業、命，於修道中方始建立。由如是等，漸次修習三十七種菩提分法加行方便，是名菩提分修。
items.en: All of this eightfold noble path is, in total, established as two kinds: non-action, and abiding action. Non-action is right speech, right action, and right livelihood. Abiding action is, further, of two kinds: calm-abiding and insight. Right view, right intention, and right effort belong to insight; right mindfulness and right concentration belong to calm-abiding. … The sudden arising of wisdom is called the path of seeing — a momentary wisdom that immediately and permanently ends every such affliction. For this reason, right speech, right action, and right livelihood are established only within the path of cultivation. … Through gradually cultivating the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and their preparatory means in this way — this is called cultivation through the factors of enlightenment.

items.title: Section: The Fruit of Cultivation Opens — Topic Thirteen of Seventeen

items.en: What is the fruit of cultivation?

items.zh: 謂四沙門果。一、預流果，二、一來果，三、不還果，四、最上阿羅漢果。此中云何名沙門？云何名果？謂聖道名沙門，煩惱斷名果。又後生道或中或上，是前生道所生之果。問：
items.en: The fruit of cultivation is the four fruits of the renunciant: the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the supreme fruit of arhatship. What here is called "renunciant"? What is called "fruit"? The noble path itself is called the renunciant; the cutting off of affliction is called the fruit. Further, a later-arising path — whether middling or supreme — is itself the fruit produced by an earlier-arising path.

items.title: Section: Why Exactly Four Fruits — Three Obstructions in Three Kinds of Person

items.zh: 何故建立如是四果？答：對治四種諸煩惱故。謂諸無事能感惡趣、往惡趣因煩惱斷故，及能斷彼對治生故，立預流果。而薄伽梵說永斷三結立此果者，謂依三品，有三種結，障礙聖道令不生故。一、在家品，二、惡說法毘奈耶品，三、善說法毘奈耶品。依在家品，有薩迦耶見。由此見故，先生怖畏，最初不欲發趣聖道。依惡說法毘奈耶品，有戒禁取。由此取故，雖已發趣，而行邪僻。由是不能生起聖道。依善說法毘奈耶品，有疑。由此疑故，雖已發趣，不行邪僻，而於正道未串習故，於如實見所知事中猶預疑惑，障礙聖道不令生起。
items.en: Why are exactly these four fruits established? Answer: because they counter four kinds of affliction. … Belonging to the category of the householder, there is the view of a substantial self; because of this view, fear arises beforehand, and one has no wish, from the very start, to set out towards the noble path. Belonging to the category of those following a poorly-taught teaching and discipline, there is attachment to rites and rituals; because of this attachment, though one has already set out, one's conduct is deviant and false, and so the noble path cannot arise. Belonging to the category of those following a well-taught teaching and discipline, there is doubt; because of this doubt, though one has set out and one's conduct is not deviant, one has not yet thoroughly practised the true path, and so, wavering and doubting regarding what is directly seen to be known, the noble path is obstructed from arising.

items.zh: 由是因緣，唯說斷此，立預流果。此預流果極餘七有，由是因緣，多生相續。

items.title: Section: The Remaining Three Fruits Close; the Fruit of Cultivation Named in Full

items.zh: 若斷再生相續煩惱，生無重續，立一來果。謂若永斷天有所攝、人有所攝再生相續所有煩惱，極唯更受天有一生、人有一生，故於爾時立一來果。若已永斷能感還來生此煩惱，唯於天有當可受生，即於爾時立不還果。若已永斷一切能感生有煩惱，建立最上阿羅漢果。而薄伽梵說：永斷三結，縛貪瞋癡，立一來果。永斷能順五下分結，立不還果。永斷一切煩惱究竟，建立最上阿羅漢果。是名修果。
items.en: If one has cut off the affliction that leads to repeated rebirth here, such that birth no longer continues again and again, the fruit of once-returning is established. … If one has already permanently cut off the affliction that would cause a return to birth here, with only heavenly rebirth still to come, at that time the fruit of non-returning is established. If one has already permanently cut off every affliction capable of producing further existence, the supreme fruit of arhatship is established. And the Bhagavān said: with the three knots permanently cut and craving, aversion, and delusion thinned, the fruit of once-returning is established; with what accords with the five lower fetters permanently cut, the fruit of non-returning is established; with every affliction permanently and completely exhausted, the supreme fruit of arhatship is established. This is called the fruit of cultivation.

blocks.text: The eightfold path closes, completing the thirty-seven factors. Then the thirteenth question: what is the fruit of cultivation?

Right speech, action, and livelihood are called "precepts loved by the noble", because the noble "have long delighted in, longed for, and taken joy in them". Such a one "never again knowingly speaks falsehood". The teachers discuss a case: one who in absorption truly saw that it would rain in seven days, and said so; conditions changed and it did not rain. Because it was said sincerely, as it was seen, it is not a "knowing" falsehood.

The path has two parts: "non-action" (right speech, action, livelihood: refraining) and "abiding action" (the other five). The first three are established only on the path of cultivation, not at the moment of seeing.

"The fruit of cultivation is the four fruits of the renunciant." "The noble path itself is called the renunciant; the cutting off of affliction is called the fruit." And "a later-arising path is itself the fruit of an earlier one".

Because they counter four kinds of affliction. For the householder, identity view; for those of other teachings, attachment to rules and rituals; for those in the Buddha's teaching, doubt. Cutting these three is stream-entry. Cutting the affliction that leads to repeated rebirth here is once-returning; "with only heavenly rebirth still to come", non-returning; cutting all, arhatship.

quiz.q: With the noble-loved precepts one "never knowingly speaks falsehood." The lectures cite Maudgalyāyana predicting rain that didn't come. What is the criterion?
options: whether one speaks knowingly false: he spoke sincerely; conditions changed, so it was no lie
quiz.why: "One never again knowingly speaks falsehood." Master Cháng Bǎi: "In absorption I truly observed that it would rain in seven days, but conditions changed." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I spoke with a sincere mind — I believed it would rain in seven days."

quiz.q: This treatise sets right speech, action, and livelihood only in the path of cultivation. How do the masters compare other treatises?
options: here: factors at seeing, path at cultivation; Cháng Bǎi notes the Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra and Kośa reverse it
quiz.why: "For this reason, right speech, right action, and right livelihood are established only within the path of cultivation." Venerable Miào Jìng: in this text, the seven factors belong to seeing, the eightfold path to cultivation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra and the Kośa place the eightfold path at seeing and the seven factors at cultivation.

quiz.q: What is the fruit of cultivation, and how does it relate to the thirty-seven factors?
options: the four renunciant fruits; the 37 factors are the cause, cultivating them yields the fruit
quiz.why: "The fruit of cultivation is the four fruits of the renunciant: stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and supreme arhatship." Venerable Miào Jìng: the thirty-seven factors are the cause; cultivating them yields a fruit — what fruit?

quiz.q: "The noble path is called the renunciant." What other translation of śramaṇa does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: "diligent stilling" — diligently cultivating the path and stilling greed, hatred, delusion
quiz.why: "The noble path itself is called the renunciant; the cutting off of affliction is called the fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: a second translation is "diligent stilling" — diligently cultivating the path and stilling all greed, hatred, and delusion.

quiz.q: "後生道 … is the fruit of 前生道" is rendered "later-arising path." How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng reads 生 as lifetime — the path attained in a later life; Cháng Bǎi: progressive attainment, not arhatship at once
quiz.why: "Further, a later-arising path — whether middling or supreme — is itself the fruit produced by an earlier-arising path." Venerable Miào Jìng: "later-arising path" is the path attained in a later life — whether middling grade… Master Cháng Bǎi: it is progressive attainment, not reaching ultimate arhatship all at once. The English "later-arising" takes only the sense of sequence.

quiz.q: Householders have self-view; with what result, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi relate view to attainment?
options: fear arises and one won't set out; conduct never exceeds one's view — attainment matches view
quiz.why: "Belonging to the category of the householder, there is the view of a substantial self; because of this view, fear arises beforehand, and one has no wish to set out towards the noble path." Master Cháng Bǎi: one's conduct never exceeds one's thought and view; as high as one's view, so great one's attainment.

quiz.q: Once-returning: "生無重續" is rendered "birth no longer continues without end." How do the lectures read it?
options: Miào Jìng: one return to the human realm, one to heaven; Cháng Bǎi: at most one heavenly and one human life; "without end" drifts from the sense
quiz.why: "If one has cut off the affliction that leads to repeated rebirth here, such that birth no longer continues without end, the fruit of once-returning is established." Venerable Miào Jìng: "coming" means one coming to the human world and one going to heaven. Master Cháng Bǎi: having cut six grades of desire-realm affliction, at most one more heavenly and one human life, then nirvāṇa. "Without end" shifts the meaning.
